headline: Comparative genomics traces gene repertoires, codon selection and transposon-derived exons
label: Comparative Genome Architecture Inference
summary: Genome-scale comparative datasets now resolve gene-family evolution, codon-level selection and transposon-derived splice isoforms.
synthesis: The three studies share a comparative framework in which large sequence collections are used to infer how gene families and genomic elements evolved. The vertebrate Wnt study analyzes 38,886 sequences from 1,961 vertebrates, quantifying copy-number variation, WGD effects and dN/dS rates. The avian CYP4 study applies site, branch and branch-site codon models across four subfamilies in 363 genomes to link selection patterns to lineage-specific evolution. The Drosophila study addresses a different question: an improved TEChim analysis indicates that intronic transposons form alternative exons in brain isoforms, rebutting Azad et al. The dominant thread is comparative inference of gene repertoire and selection across genomes. What is new is extending this approach from gene-family and codon-level evolution to transposon contributions to transcript structure.
